utility.notes: Suisun City is a well-documented Solano County city within PG&E's core Northern California service territory.

value.name: Pacific Gas & Electric (PG&E)
value.notes: Directly re-verified this session via MCE's own service-area page, which explicitly lists its Solano County service as exactly four communities: Benicia, Fairfield, Vallejo, and unincorporated Solano County. Suisun City is not among them, and no other CCA was found serving Solano County. PG&E is recorded as both the distribution and generation utility.

interconnection_url.notes: PG&E's own utility-wide Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across PG&E's entire distribution territory, which includes Suisun City/Solano County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.

value.name: Checklist adopted by the Building Official, substantially conforming to the California Solar Permitting Guidebook

required_documents.notes: Per Suisun City Municipal Code Section 15.04.390(E): the Building Official adopts a checklist for small residential rooftop solar energy systems substantially conforming to the California Solar Permitting Guidebook; the code text itself does not itemize further documents beyond this checklist.

value: Inspections may be requested by calling 707-421-7319 or through the online permit portal; scheduling is the responsibility of the permittee
The inspection card must be on-site at the time of inspection
No work beyond the point of each successive inspection may proceed without prior approval from the Building Division
inspection_steps.notes: This is the City's general Building Division inspection process (the same page covers all building permit types, including solar); the City does not publish a separate, solar-specific inspection sequence.

value.notes: Suisun City Municipal Code Section 15.04.390(F)(1): 'The building official shall issue a building permit or other nondiscretionary permit the same day for applications that meet the requirements of the approved checklist or within three business days for electronic applications after receipt of a complete application.'

value.program_or_pathway: Standard solar permitting under the city's Renewable Energy-Solar ordinance (Chapter 18.60)
other_conditions: Applies to all zoning districts in the city except Open Space (OS)
Solar panels and solar thermal tanks must be mounted no more than 10 inches from the roof surface
Based on the city's latitude, fixed-angle solar panels should be mounted at a 31-32 degree angle to horizontal
